record.context_brief: Branch-space representations of ordered real subsets
record.original_question: Let < be the usual ordering of the real line. For which subsets X of R does there exist a tree T, together with linear orderings of the nodes of T, such that no node of T contains an order-isomorphic copy of (X,<), while (X,<) itself is order-isomorphic to the branch space of T? In particular, which F_sigma_delta subsets of R are order-isomorphic to the branch space of some countable tree?

evidence.quote: Question 19 ([13]). Let < be the usual ordering of R. For which subsets X ⊆ R is there a tree T and linear orderings of the nodes of T so that (a) no node of T contains an order isomorphic copy of (X, <), and (b) (X, <) is order isomorphic to the branch space of T? (Both R and P are representable in this way, but Q is not.) Which Fσδ-subsets of R are order isomorphic to the branch space of some countable tree?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $<$ denote the usual ordering of the real line $\mathbb{R}$. A tree is a partially ordered set $(T,\le_T)$ in which, for every $t\in T$, the set of predecessors $\{s\in T : s<_T t\}$ is well-ordered by $<_T$. A node of $T$ is a maximal antichain consisting of elements that all have the same set of strict predecessors (equivalently, the set of immediate successors of a fixed element together with the set of minimal elements forms the nodes). A branch of $T$ is a maximal linearly ordered subset of $T$. Suppose each node of $T$ is endowed with a linear ordering; then the set $B(T)$ of all branches of $T$ carries the lexicographic linear ordering induced by these node orderings, in which two distinct branches $b_1,b_2$ are compared by looking at the unique node containing both their splitting elements and using the linear order on that node. This linearly ordered set $B(T)$ is called the branch space of $T$.

(a) Characterize those subsets $X\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ for which there exists a tree $T$ together with linear orderings of the nodes of $T$ such that:
 (i) no node of $T$ contains, as a linearly ordered subset, a copy order-isomorphic to $(X,<)$; and
 (ii) $(X,<)$ is order-isomorphic to the branch space $B(T)$ of $T$.

(b) In particular, characterize precisely which $F_{\sigma\delta}$-subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ (i.e., subsets that are countable intersections of $F_\sigma$ sets in $\mathbb{R}$) are order-isomorphic to the branch space of some countable tree $T$ (with linearly ordered nodes).

It is known that both $\mathbb{R}$ and the space of irrationals $\mathbb{P}$ admit such representations, while the rationals $\mathbb{Q}$ do not.
artifact.category_tag: Linearly ordered topological spaces and branch spaces of trees
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed in the collection "Open Problems in Topology II". Work by Bennett, Lutzer, and Rudin ("Lines, Trees, and Branch Spaces"; "Branch Space Representations of Lines") provides necessary conditions (e.g., subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ representable as branch spaces of trees with countable nodes must be $F_{\sigma\delta}$ and must be either $\alpha$-favorable or contain a non-empty countable open set) and representations for $\mathbb{R}$ and the irrationals, but a complete characterization of representable subsets and of representable $F_{\sigma\delta}$ subsets via countable trees does not appear to have been established. The problem appears to remain open with only partial results.

status_evidence.title: Branch Space Representations of Lines
status_evidence.snippet: If a subset X of the real numbers is order isomorphic to the branch space of a tree T having countable nodes, then X is an F_sigma_delta-subset of the real line and there is a countable subtree U of T such that X is order isomorphic to the branch space of U.
status_evidence.claim: Provides necessary conditions (F_sigma_delta) and partial structural results, but does not give a full characterization.

status_evidence.title: Lines, Trees, and Branch Spaces (Order 19, 367–384, 2002)
status_evidence.snippet: Examines the interactions between the topology of certain LOTS and the properties of trees in whose branch spaces they embed.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial results on which lines arise as branch spaces of trees.
